question: Does primary prior art state growing-subsystem entropy/trace/Petz-chi-square testing windows for rho_N proportional to exp(2 J^2/N), with J=sum_i sigma_i/2, on the full tensor Hilbert space?
conclusion_boundary: Exact model and global critical magnetization law located; exact growing-marginal threshold not located in this bounded search. This is not novelty or priority clearance.

external_sources.title: Quantum spins and random loops on the complete graph
external_sources.version: v2, last revised 2019-11-20; arXiv record checked 2026-10-08

read_spans.content: Complete-graph spin-S tensor Hilbert space, standard spin Casimir, isotropic Hamiltonian H=-(2/n) sum_{i<j} S_i dot S_j, and full-trace Gibbs functional.
Spin-1/2 critical inverse temperature beta_c=2; global magnetization exponential-moment limit for all complex h.

read_spans.location: HTML lines 468-508, Section 4, Proposition 4.1 and proof of Theorem 2.1
read_spans.content: Multiplicity-difference generating function, saddle-point estimate, total-spin sum and Laplace-ratio proof.

assumptions_and_scope: Fixed beta and h in C for the order-parameter limit
external_sources.normalization_reconstruction: For S_i=sigma_i/2, J=sum_i S_i and J^2=(3n/4)I+2 sum_{i<j}S_i dot S_j; hence H=-(2/n)sum pair=-J^2/n+(3/4)I. Scalar cancels from Gibbs normalization, so beta=2 matches the target exactly.
external_sources.known_limitations: The theorem is a thermodynamic limit for a global magnetization exponential moment; it gives no r_N-growing partial-trace trace/entropy/Petz-chi-square window or finite-size critical local error bound.

external_sources.title: Reduced density matrix and entanglement entropy of permutationally invariant quantum many-body systems

read_spans.content: Complete-graph spin-half Heisenberg example with fixed S_z=L/2-N, eigenstate label r, degeneracy binomial difference, and maximally mixed density on a degenerate eigenspace.
Subsystem RDM defined by partial trace from L sites to an arbitrary n-site subsystem.
Permutation-irrep block reduction and RDM eigenvalues as finite linear combinations of block entries.
Thermal RDM is averaged over symmetry sectors at fixed polarization; cited leading entropy scaling across the phase transition.

assumptions_and_scope: Thermal sum over permutation/Young sectors within the fixed-polarization sector
external_sources.known_limitations: Not the full zero-field Gibbs trace over all N magnetization sectors. Entropy-density asymptotics do not determine o(1) relative-entropy deficit, trace distance, or the target square-root window.

external_sources.title: Spectral Gap of the Davies Generator for the Mean-Field Heisenberg Model
external_sources.version: v1, submitted 2026-07-23; arXiv version history checked 2026-10-08 lists v1 only

read_spans.content: Displayed Hamiltonian and Davies spectral-gap theorem, including stated beta_c=2.
Schur-Weyl decomposition with spin irrep dimension and multiplicity dimension.
Single-qubit Casimir 3/4 and exact Hamiltonian/Casimir relation from Eq. (1.1).
Stationary sector law with dim(Pi_s) and binomial-difference multiplicity formula.

external_sources.normalization_boundary: Under the explicit Casimir convention in Appendix A, Eq. (A.17) gives H=3I/8-(1/(2n))sum_s s(s+1)Pi_s. Proposition 2.3 Eq. (2.8) and Eq. (D.8) instead use the doubled coefficient 1/n after noting 'up to a shift and rescaling.' Do not transplant beta=2 to the target from Eq. (1.1) without resolving this factor.
external_sources.full_hilbert_sector_weight: dim(Pi_s)=(2s+1)*m_{n,s}, m_{n,s}=binom(n,n/2-s)-binom(n,n/2-s-1) for s<n/2; m_{n,n/2}=1. Eq. (D.8) weights by dim(Pi_s), not a lone binomial.
external_sources.known_limitations: The main theorem concerns Davies-generator spectral gaps, not growing subsystem marginals or local distinguishability.
